- Uniform white, powdery coating over the leaf surface
- Leaf tissue structure appears intact (no necrotic lesions or holes)
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight, Target Spot)
- No water-soaked blotches (rules out Late Blight, Bacterial diseases)
- No yellowing halos or small circular spots (rules out Septoria)
- The powdery white growth is the dominant feature

**Matching to classes:**
- **Powdery Mildew** — perfectly matches: "White, powdery sporulation on both the tops and undersides of leaves, in round spots that begin small but expand and converge; entire leaves wither and die but remain attached." The uniform whitish/powdery appearance covering the leaf is the hallmark signature of powdery mildew.
